Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (6) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. A retry can start two leads 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>start_lead() returns exit 1 when fire() times out or receives a response it cannot recognize,
>even though the task may already have started a session. The handover instructions tell the lead to
>retry immediately, while no lease or LEAD-STARTED marker necessarily exists to stop the second
>fire.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3768-3772]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3768-R3772) > >```diff >+ if status == 0: >+ return 1, f"lead task not started: {answer}" >+ detail = answer_detail(answer, token) >+ what = f"HTTP {status}" if status != 200 else "HTTP 200 without routine_fire" >+ return 1, f"lead task not started: {what}" + (f": {detail}" if detail else "") >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Retry-after-timeout duplicate start is a semantic reliability concern. Only undetermined PR 8
>feedback on a related handoff path; no closely matching precedent.
>
> > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The request contains a join line but no idempotency key. Curl failures become status 0, which the
>caller maps to retryable exit 1; the duplicate guard depends on a held lease or a posted start
>marker, neither of which is guaranteed before the first session joins.
>
> > [room.py\[3631-3651\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3631-L3651) > [room.py\[3691-3707\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3691-L3707) > [room.py\[3755-3772\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3755-L3772) > [LEAD.md\[323-334\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/LEAD.md/#L323-L334) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A timed-out or unrecognized fire response can follow a successful server-side start. Returning a retryable failure can start a second lead before the first joins. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3636-3651] >- room.py[3768-3772] >- LEAD.md[328-334] >## Recommended Fix >Distinguish definitively rejected requests from requests with an unknown outcome. Do not instruct callers to fire again immediately after an unknown outcome; first reconcile whether a session started, or use an API-supported idempotency mechanism if available. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/7d6654d2-d118-4349-8aec-fd7579b30aa1?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/7d6654d2-d118-4349-8aec-fd7579b30aa1)
2. Unrecorded starts can spawn another lead 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>start_lead() reports a successful fire even when post_quietly() fails to record LEAD-STARTED,
>leaving the watchdog without its record of the new session. If the next watchdog run occurs before
>that session posts LEAD ONLINE, it can fire another takeover for the same stall; the architect's
>new instructions also treat an absent marker as a reason to start one by hand.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3759-3763]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3759-R3763) > >```diff >+ err = post_quietly(room, role, f"LEAD-STARTED: {url} ({'takeover' if takeover else 'plain'} join line, " >+ f"started by {role}" + (f" after {after})" if after else ")"), a) >+ if err: >+ print(f"started, but LEAD-STARTED wasn't posted: {one_line(err, token)}") >+ return 0, None >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Unrecorded LEAD-STARTED and duplicate-takeover risk is reliability-semantic. No dismissals or
>rejections found; accepted PR 8 handoff-failure feedback is only undetermined. Uncertain.
>
> > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The test confirms that a successful fire can leave no comment and still return zero. Episode start
>counts and the recent-start guard read room markers, while the architect procedure directs a
>takeover when one is absent.
>
> > [tests/test_relay.py\[482-491\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/tests/test_relay.py/#L482-L491) > [room.py\[3755-3763\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3755-L3763) > [room.py\[2997-3031\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L2997-L3031) > [room.py\[3696-3707\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3696-L3707) > [ARCHITECT.md\[404-409\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/ARCHITECT.md/#L404-L409) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A successful task fire can leave no durable start marker when the room post fails. The watchdog and architect can then mistake a starting session for a failed fire. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3755-3763] >- room.py[2997-3031] >- ARCHITECT.md[404-409] >## Recommended Fix >Retry or reconcile the marker post after a confirmed fire, and prevent unattended refiring while that successful start remains unrecorded. Make the architect verify whether a session or lease appeared before treating a missing marker as proof that no lead started. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/24de4422-3be3-4c2c-a160-c919ff1e518b?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/24de4422-3be3-4c2c-a160-c919ff1e518b)

3. Buzz instructions can start a second lead 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The revised LEAD-SILENT instructions say the architect may start the takeover itself or give
>Matthew a takeover line, but the next step tells Matthew to start a lead unconditionally. If the
>architect already fired the task, following both steps can launch another takeover instead of
>stopping after the first start.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/manual/answer-a-buzz.md[99]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-d3a70a640b14f1436419811a13d5e127a067c49ce42446d9f02bf5cbe82b2419R99-R99) > >```diff >+4. If no takeover lead came online, the architect starts a takeover lead itself, or gives you the **takeover line**. The watchdog sees that start and holds off (three hours, by default), so the two don't collide. It ends with "Take over the lease … the previous lead stopped without handing over." >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Trivial doc contradiction: alternatives at step 4 conflict with unconditional start at step 6.
>Fixing wording is a low-risk clarity change; no rejection precedent.
>
> > [PR-#9](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The alternatives appear at step 4, followed by an unconditional start at step 6. The separate
>hand-start manual already tells Matthew to skip to the expected-result section when the architect
>starts the lead.
>
> > [docs/manual/answer-a-buzz.md\[98-101\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/docs/manual/answer-a-buzz.md/#L98-L101) > [docs/manual/start-the-next-lead-by-hand.md\[33-38\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/docs/manual/start-the-next-lead-by-hand.md/#L33-L38) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The buzz procedure offers an architect-started takeover but then directs Matthew to start another one regardless. >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/manual/answer-a-buzz.md[98-101] >## Recommended Fix >Make the final start step conditional on receiving a takeover line. If the architect starts the lead, direct Matthew to wait for that lead instead. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/81dfe293-bf09-4ef0-8a9b-91d1609ba799?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/81dfe293-bf09-4ef0-8a9b-91d1609ba799)
4. Other processes can read the fire token 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>fire() embeds the bearer token in the curl argument vector rather than passing it through a
>protected input channel. On a host where another local process can inspect process arguments during
>the request, that process can copy the credential used to fire the project's lead task.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3631-3633]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3631-R3633) > >```diff >+ cmd = ["curl", "-sS", "-m", str(FIRE_TIMEOUT), "-X", "POST", >+ "-H", f"Authorization: Bearer {token}", "-H", f"anthropic-beta: {beta}", >+ "-H", "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01", "-H", "Content-Type: application/json", >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Credential exposure concern is a security theme the team accepted in PR 9 (survey brief secrets),
>but no precedent covers curl argv tokens specifically.
>
> > [PR-#9](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The token comes from the environment and is interpolated into a -H argument passed to
>subprocess.run; the manual identifies it as the credential for this task's API trigger.
>
> > [room.py\[3612-3618\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3612-L3618) > [room.py\[3626-3637\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3626-L3637) > [docs/manual/set-up-the-lead-task.md\[39-60\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/docs/manual/set-up-the-lead-task.md/#L39-L60) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The fire token appears in curl's process arguments during every request, despite being scrubbed from printed output. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3626-3641] >## Recommended Fix >Pass the authorization header to curl through a protected stdin-fed configuration or another mechanism that does not place the token in the command-line arguments. Preserve output and error scrubbing. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/9b65adbb-0dd1-4bb2-b7cf-f6988f89942a?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/9b65adbb-0dd1-4bb2-b7cf-f6988f89942a)
5. A failed post-decision lead leaves the room silent forever 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>pending_decision skips a DECISION-n as soon as any trusted LEAD-STARTED is newer than it.
>After that, cmd_watchdog prints quiet: step is waiting for owner… on every later run, because
>the step is still waiting for owner and the lease is still released. So if the lead started after
>the decision (by the watchdog or the architect) never joins, for example because its session ended
>at once, ran out of usage, or the fire returned 200 but the run died, the watchdog never alarms and
>never starts another lead, and the room stalls with no buzz until someone reads it by hand.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3057-3061]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3057-R3061) > >```diff >+ if t is None or now - t <= DECISION_GRACE: >+ continue >+ if any(m["id"] > d["id"] and message_kind(m["text"]) == "LEAD-STARTED" for m in msgs): >+ continue >+ return d >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Substantive watchdog reliability logic. No dismissals or rejections for this path; accepted
>watchdog-progress feedback exists but this is a semantic change. Uncertain.
>
> > [PR-#5](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5) > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Trace: the parked lead set waiting for owner and released the lease. The DECISION is posted, and
>after 30 minutes the watchdog fires and posts LEAD-STARTED … after DECISION-n. The started session
>never reaches lease take or LEAD ONLINE. On the next run quiet_reason returns ('waiting', …)
>because the step is waiting and the holder is none. pending_decision reaches the `any(...
>LEAD-STARTED ...) check, hits continue, and returns None. cmd_watchdog` then prints quiet and
>returns 0. Nothing else in the watchdog looks at this state: the stall/alarm path is only reached
>when quiet_reason returns None. start_refusal's 30-minute 'still starting' window shows the code
>already treats a LEAD-STARTED with no LEAD ONLINE as stale after 30 minutes, but pending_decision
>treats it as final. ARCHITECT.md only covers this case if the architect happens to check in by hand.
>
> > [room.py\[3042-3062\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3042-L3062) > [room.py\[2781-2807\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L2781-L2807) > [room.py\[3146-3159\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3146-L3159) > [room.py\[3696-3706\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3696-L3706) > [ARCHITECT.md\[430-431\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/ARCHITECT.md/#L430-L431) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`pending_decision` treats any LEAD-STARTED after a DECISION as answering it for good. If that lead never posts LEAD ONLINE, the room stays at `waiting for owner` with the lease released, and the watchdog stays quiet forever. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3042-3062] >- room.py[3146-3159] > >## Recommended Fix >In `pending_decision`, ignore a LEAD-STARTED after the decision when it is older than `STARTING_FOR` (or `a.silent_after`) and no trusted lead LEAD ONLINE follows it. Cap such retries, for example at two decision starts per DECISION, then post one LEAD-SILENT (within ALARM_CAP) saying the lead started after DECISION-n never joined. Add a test: parked room, DECISION older than 30 min, watchdog LEAD-STARTED older than 30 min with no LEAD ONLINE. The watchdog should start again or alarm, not stay quiet. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/8465c611-9314-4999-b33b-4e15f26bec79?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/8465c611-9314-4999-b33b-4e15f26bec79)
View medium (1)
6. Watchdog can take over from a working lead 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_watchdog passes takeover=lease_of(values)[0] != "none" to alarm_stage, which calls
>watchdog_start as soon as silent_after has passed since the last LEAD-STARTED or LEAD ONLINE.
>Nothing checks whether the lease holder is still alive. Progress counts only step and pr changes,
>mission-branch pushes and merges, so a live lead whose builders run past three hours with no merge
>is enough to trigger it. The takeover lead runs lease take --takeover and the working lead loses
>the lease mid-build. Before this PR the watchdog only alarmed, and the architect checked whether the
>lead was alive before giving out a takeover line.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3193-3195]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/11/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3193-R3195) > >```diff >+ alarm_stage(a, ep, (f"no progress for {span(now - progress)} ({what} at {iso(progress)})", >+ f"LEAD-SILENT: no progress since {iso(progress)} (step {step}, mission {mission})"), >+ f"step {step}, mission {mission}", takeover=lease_of(values)[0] != "none") >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Automatic takeover while lead may be alive is risky. Accepted PR 5 asked for watchdog progress
>signals, so the team cares about this path, but no close precedent decides it.
>
> > [PR-#5](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>alarm_stage sets due = not a.no_start and now - ep['sign'] >= a.silent_after. sign comes only
>from LEAD-STARTED and lead LEAD ONLINE messages, so it does not change while a lead is working. On
>the first alarm it calls watchdog_start(a, takeover) with takeover True whenever the lease is
>held. LEAD.md lets a lead run up to three background builders and end its turn while they run,
>posting nothing that counts as progress. The old flow (start-the-next-lead-by-hand.md, ARCHITECT.md)
>had the architect confirm the lead was gone before a takeover; the automatic start skips that check.
>
> > [room.py\[2997-3039\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L2997-L3039) > [room.py\[3185-3196\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/room.py/#L3185-L3196) > [LEAD.md\[105-106\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/LEAD.md/#L105-L106) > [LEAD.md\[161\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/cde42bac28cebb6f54ade74bed236467aef6e605/LEAD.md/#L161-L161) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The watchdog starts a takeover lead as soon as `silent_after` has passed with no step, pr or branch progress. It does this even when the lease holder is alive and waiting on long-running builders, and the takeover takes the lease from a working lead. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2997-3039] >- room.py[3185-3196] > >## Recommended Fix >Count the lease holder's recent trusted lead messages (for example any lead STATUS or other lead message from the lease holder's session) as a sign of a lead in `stall_episode`'s `sign`, or delay the first takeover start until one alarm interval after the first LEAD-SILENT. That gives a live lead the chance to answer with a STATUS, as LEAD.md asks. Add a test where the holder posts a STATUS after the alarm: the watchdog should not start a takeover. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/42dd4705-8671-4c77-a008-0f46c9491078?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/42dd4705-8671-4c77-a008-0f46c9491078)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
